record.context_brief: Non-uniqueness with codirected terminal edges in d>=3
record.original_question: Let A \subset \mathbb{R}^d be compact. The Steiner problem considered here is: find a closed set St of minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H^1(St)) such that St \cup A is connected; such a minimizer is called a Steiner set, and if St is connected it is called a Steiner tree (in particular, this holds when A is finite). For dimensions d \ge 3, does there exist a finite set of terminals A such that there are two different Steiner trees St_1 and St_2 connecting A, but the directions of all segments incident to terminals are the same (equivalently, the two trees coincide in a neighborhood of the terminals)?

evidence.quote:
For a given compact set A ⊂ Rd find a closed set St with minimal length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure H1 ) such
that St ∪ A is connected. We will call such a solution St Steiner set. If St is connected (which is the case if A is finite or
totally disconnected) we call it Steiner tree.

Question 2.1. Does there exist a finite set of terminals in Rd , d ≥ 3 with two different Steiner trees St1 and St2 such
that the directions of all segments incident to terminals are the same (in other words trees coincide in a neighborhood of
terminals)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a compact set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, the Steiner problem asks for a closed set $\mathrm{St}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\mathrm{St})$ such that $\mathrm{St}\cup A$ is connected. Such a minimizer is called a Steiner set; when $\mathrm{St}$ is connected (in particular whenever $A$ is finite) it is called a Steiner tree connecting $A$. It is a classical fact that any Steiner tree connecting a finite set $A$ is a finite union of straight segments meeting only at points of $A$ (terminals) or at additional Steiner points, and that each terminal has at least one segment incident to it.

Question: For some dimension $d\ge 3$, does there exist a finite set $A\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting two distinct Steiner trees $\mathrm{St}_1$ and $\mathrm{St}_2$ connecting $A$ such that, at every terminal $a\in A$, the set of unit directions of segments of $\mathrm{St}_1$ incident to $a$ equals the set of unit directions of segments of $\mathrm{St}_2$ incident to $a$ (equivalently, $\mathrm{St}_1$ and $\mathrm{St}_2$ coincide in a neighborhood of $A$)?
artifact.status_search_result: In the plane, Oblakov's theorem rules out two distinct locally minimal Steiner trees that are codirected at all terminals. The corresponding question in dimensions $d\ge 3$ is stated as an open problem in current surveys of open problems on Steiner trees, with no known resolution.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: In the plane, K. Oblakov has proved that it is impossible, but all possible generalizations to higher dimensions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The codirected non-uniqueness question in dimensions d>=3 is listed as an open problem.
